chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) about a group of people who bought cloth (baz̄) and jointly owned it together but had not yet divided it. Is it permissible for any one of them to sell his share of the cloth before taking possession (qabḍ)? He said, 'There is no harm in it.' And he said, 'For this is not in the same category as food, because food is measured by volume/weight (mukālah).'

key_terms.الطَّعَام: Food (specifically staple grains/food in this context)
key_terms.يُكَالُ: Is measured by volume (as opposed to being weighed or counted)

ai.seo_question: Can I sell my share of a bulk purchase before dividing it?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) permitted selling a share of jointly owned cloth before physical division, distinguishing it from food which requires measurement (mukālah) to avoid uncertainty (gharar). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the requirement for possession (qabd) varies by commodity type, allowing for greater commercial flexibility with non-perishable goods like textiles compared to consumables. The hadith underscores the practical application of gharar avoidance in medieval trade, reflecting the nuanced legal reasoning found in Shaykh al-Tusi’s Tahdhib al-Ahkam.
